questions.question_text: Which built-in role allows read-only access to all resources in a subscription?
questions.explanation: The Reader built-in role provides read-only permissions across the subscription, according to the Azure documentation at docs.microsoft.com.

questions.question_text: When assigning a role at a resource group scope, which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The assignment applies to the resource group resource.

options.label: B
options.text: The assignment applies to all resources within the resource group.

options.label: C
options.text: The assignment applies to the management group.

options.label: D
options.text: The assignment applies to the subscription root.

questions.explanation: The role assignment at a resource group scope applies to every resource that belongs to that group, according to the Azure RBAC documentation.

questions.question_text: A developer needs to grant a service principal permission to read Azure Key Vault secrets but not manage the vault itself. Which built-in role should be assigned?
questions.explanation: The Key Vault Reader role grants read access to secrets while preventing management actions on the vault, which matches the requirement described in the Azure docs.

questions.question_text: You have a subscription scoped role assignment for Reader at the subscription level. Which scope(s) will inherit this assignment?

options.label: A
options.text: All resource groups in the subscription.

questions.explanation: A subscription-level assignment is inherited by all resources, resource groups, and other objects under that subscription, per the RBAC inheritance rules in the Azure guide.

questions.question_text: An administrator wants to assign a custom role that includes the Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write permission at a management group scope. Which approach is required?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign a built-in role at the management group scope.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a custom role that includes the required permission and assign it at the management group scope.

options.label: C
options.text: Use Azure AD role assignment to grant the permission.

options.label: D
options.text: Assign the Owner role at the subscription scope.

questions.explanation: Creating a custom role that includes the specific permission and assigning it at the management group scope follows the process outlined in the Azure documentation for custom role definitions and scope assignment.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the precedence of role assignments when multiple assignments exist at different scopes for the same user?

options.label: A
options.text: The assignment with the highest level of restriction takes precedence.

options.label: B
options.text: The assignment with the lowest level of restriction takes precedence.

options.label: C
options.text: Assignments are merged and the most permissive wins.

options.label: D
options.text: The most recent assignment overrides earlier ones.

questions.explanation: When multiple role assignments exist, the one that imposes the greatest restriction is evaluated first, which is explained in the Azure RBAC precedence guidance.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command would you use to view effective access for a user on a specific resource?
questions.explanation: The az role assignment show-effective-access command returns the effective permissions for the specified principal on the given resource, as detailed in the Azure CLI reference.

questions.question_text: Which Azure portal blade is used to manage built-in roles?
questions.explanation: The Access control (IAM) blade in the Azure portal is where built-in role management is performed, according to the Azure portal navigation guide.

questions.question_text: A company wants to assign a role to a user such that the user can manage virtual machines within a specific resource group. Which scope should be used?
questions.explanation: Assigning a role at the resource group scope limits the permissions to resources inside that group, which aligns with the RBAC scoping recommendations in the Azure docs.

questions.question_text: You need to assign a role to a user that includes the Microsoft.Resources/deployments/write permission for a specific resource group. Which approach ensures least privilege?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign the built-in Contributor role at the subscription scope.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a custom role that includes the permission and assign it at the resource group scope.

options.label: C
options.text: Assign the Owner role at the resource group scope.

options.label: D
options.text: Assign the Reader role at the resource group scope.

questions.explanation: Creating a custom role that includes the specific permission and assigning it at the resource group scope limits the scope to that group, following the least‑privilege guidance in the Azure documentation.
